Vnde rex eos exosos habebat quod non potuissent eum templis uel imaginibus onorare huius rei gratia arbitror herodem in suos quidem feuissimum, in extraneos uero munificum paruisse.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.English:
<tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Chapter-5-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="136"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num136" xml:id="english-book16-num136" id="english-book16-num136" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="10" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" hidden="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[136]</tei-num> ABOUT this time it was that Cesarea Sebaste, which he had built, was finished. The entire building being accomplished: in the tenth year, the solemnity of it fell into the twenty-eighth year of Herod's reign, and into the hundred and ninety-second olympiad. There was accordingly a great festival and most sumptuous preparations made presently, in order to its dedication; for he had appointed a contention in music, and games to be performed naked. He had also gotten ready a great number of those that fight single combats, and of beasts for the like purpose; horse races also, and the most chargeable of such sports and shows as used to be exhibited at Rome, and in other places. He consecrated this combat to Caesar, and ordered it to be celebrated every fifth year. He also sent all sorts of ornaments for it out of his own furniture, that it might want nothing to make it decent; nay, Julia, Caesar's wife, sent a great part of her most valuable furniture [from Rome], insomuch that he had no want of any thing. The sum of them all was estimated at five hundred talents. Now when a great multitude was come to that city to see the shows, as well as the ambassadors whom other people sent, on account of the benefits they had received from Herod, he entertained them all in the public inns, and at public tables, and with perpetual feasts; this solemnity having in the day time the diversions of the fights, and in the night time such merry meetings as cost vast sums of money, and publicly demonstrated the generosity of his soul; for in all his undertakings he was ambitious to exhibit what exceeded whatsoever had been done before of the same kind. And it is related that Caesar and Agrippa often said, that the dominions of Herod were too little for the greatness of his soul; for that he deserved to have both all the kingdom of Syria, and that of Egypt also.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num142" xml:id="english-book16-num142" id="english-book16-num142" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[142]</tei-num> After this solemnity and these festivals were over, Herod erected another city in the plain called Capharsaba, where he chose out a fit place, both for plenty of water and goodness of soil, and proper for the production of what was there planted, where a river encompassed the city itself, and a grove of the best trees for magnitude was round about it: this he named Antipatris, from his father Antipater. He also built upon another spot of ground above Jericho, of the same name with his mother, a place of great security and very pleasant for habitation, and called it Cypros. He also dedicated the finest monuments to his brother Phasaelus, on account of the great natural affection there had been between them, by erecting a tower in the city itself, not less than the tower of Pharos, which he named Phasaelus, which was at once a part of the strong defenses of the city, and a memorial for him that was deceased, because it bare his name. He also built a city of the same name in the valley of Jericho, as you go from it northward, whereby he rendered the neighboring country more fruitful by the cultivation its inhabitants introduced; and this also he called Phasaelus.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num146" xml:id="english-book16-num146" id="english-book16-num146" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[146]</tei-num> But as for his other benefits, it is impossible to reckon them up, those which he bestowed on cities, both in Syria and in Greece, and in all the places he came to in his voyages; for he seems to have conferred, and that after a most plentiful manner, what would minister to many necessities, and the building of public works, and gave them the money that was necessary to such works as wanted it, to support them upon the failure of their other revenues: but what was the greatest and most illustrious of all his works, he erected Apollo's temple at Rhodes, at his own expenses, and gave them a great number of talents of silver for the repair of their fleet. He also built the greatest part of the public edifices for the inhabitants of Nicopolis, at Actium; and for the Antiochinus, the inhabitants of the principal city of Syria, where a broad street cuts through the place lengthways, he built cloisters along it on both sides, and laid the open road with polished stone, and was of very great advantage to the inhabitants. And as to the olympic games, which were in a very low condition, by reason of the failure of their revenues, he recovered their reputation, and appointed revenues for heir maintenance, and made that solemn meeting more venerable, as to the sacrifices and other ornaments; and by reason of this vast liberality, he was generally declared in their inscriptions to be one of the perpetual managers of those games.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num150" xml:id="english-book16-num150" id="english-book16-num150" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[150]</tei-num> Now some there are who stand amazed at the diversity of Herod's nature and purposes; for when we have respect to his magnificence, and the benefits which he bestowed on all mankind, there is no possibility for even those that had the least respect for him to deny, or not openly to confess, that he had a nature vastly beneficent; but when any one looks upon the punishments he inflicted, and the injuries he did, not only to his subjects, but to his nearest relations, and takes notice of his severe and unrelenting disposition there, he will be forced to allow that he was brutish, and a stranger to all humanity; insomuch that these men suppose his nature to be different, and sometimes at contradiction with itself; but I am myself of another opinion, and imagine that the occasion of both these sort of actions was one and the same; for being a man ambitious of honor, and quite overcome by that passion, he was induced to be magnificent, wherever there appeared any hopes of a future memorial, or of reputation at present; and as his expenses were beyond his abilities, he was necessitated to be harsh to his subjects; for the persons on whom he expended his money were so many, that they made him a very bad procurer of it; and because he was conscious that he was hated by those under him, for the injuries he did them, he thought it not an easy thing to amend his offenses, for that it was inconvenient for his revenue; he therefore strove on the other side to make their ill-will an occasion of his gains. As to his own court, therefore, if any one was not very obsequious to him in his language, and would not confess himself to be his slave, or but seemed to think of any innovation in his government, he was not able to contain himself, but prosecuted his very kindred and friends, and punished them as if they were enemies and this wickedness he undertook out of a desire that he might be himself alone honored. Now for this, my assertion about that passion of his, we have the greatest evidence, by what he did to honor Caesar and Agrippa, and his other friends; for with what honors he paid his respects to them who were his superiors, the same did he desire to be paid to himself; and what he thought the most excellent present he could make another, he discovered an inclination to have the like presented to himself. But now the Jewish nation is by their law a stranger to all such things, and accustomed to prefer righteousness to glory; for which reason that nation was not agreeable to him, because it was out of their power to flatter the king's ambition with statues or temples, or any other such performances; And this seems to me to have been at once the occasion of Herod's crimes as to his own courtiers and counselors, and of his benefactions as to foreigners and those that had no relation to him.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.Greek:
<tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Chapter-5-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="136"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num136" xml:id="greek-book16-num136" id="greek-book16-num136" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="10" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" hidden="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone> Περὶ δὲ τὸν χρόνον τοῦτον συντέλειαν ἔλαβεν ἡ Καισάρεια Σεβαστή, ἣν ᾠκοδόμει δεκάτῳ μὲν ἔτει πρὸς τέλος ἐλθούσης αὐτῷ τῆς ὅλης κατασκευῆς, ἐκπεσούσης δὲ τῆς προθεσμίας εἰς ὄγδοον καὶ εἰκοστὸν ἔτος τῆς ἀρχῆς ἐπ᾽ ὀλυμπιάδος δευτέρας καὶ ἐνενηκοστῆς πρὸς ταῖς ἑκατόν.  ἦν οὖν εὐθὺς ἐν καθιερώσει μείζονες ἑορταὶ καὶ παρασκευαὶ πολυτελέσταται: κατηγγέλκει μὲν γὰρ ἀγῶνα μουσικῆς καὶ γυμνικῶν ἀθλημάτων, παρεσκευάκει δὲ πολὺ πλῆθος μονομάχων καὶ θηρίων ἵππων τε δρόμον καὶ τὰ πολυτελέστερα τῶν ἔν τε τῇ Ῥώμῃ καὶ παρ᾽ ἄλλοις τισὶν ἐπιτηδευμάτων.  ἀνετίθει δὲ καὶ τοῦτον τὸν ἀγῶνα Καίσαρι κατὰ πενταετηρίδα παρεσκευασμένος ἄγειν αὐτόν: ὁ δ᾽ αὐτῷ πᾶσαν τὴν εἰς τὰ τοιαῦτα παρασκευὴν ἀπὸ τῶν οἰκείων διεπέμπετο τὴν φιλοτιμίαν ἐπικοσμῶν.  ἰδίᾳ δὲ καὶ ἡ γυνὴ Καίσαρος Ἰουλία πολλὰ τῶν ἐκεῖ πολυτελεστάτων ἀπέστειλεν, ὡς μηδὲν ὑστερεῖν τὰ πάντα συντιμώμενα ταλάντων πεντακοσίων.  συνελθόντος δ᾽ εἰς τὴν πόλιν ὄχλου πλείονος κατὰ θεωρίαν καὶ πρεσβείας, ἃς ἔπεμπον οἱ δῆμοι δι᾽ ἃς ἐπεπόνθεισαν εὐεργεσίας, ἅπαντας ἐξεδέξατο καὶ καταγωγαῖς καὶ τραπέζαις καὶ διηνεκέσιν ἑορταῖς, τῆς πανηγύρεως ἐν μὲν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐχούσης τὰς ἀπὸ τῶν θεαμάτων ψυχαγωγίας, ἐν δὲ ταῖς νυξὶ τὰς εὐφροσύνας καὶ τὴν εἰς τοῦτο πολυτέλειαν, ὡς ἐπίσημον γενέσθαι τὴν μεγαλοψυχίαν αὐτοῦ:  εἰς πάντα γὰρ ἅπερ ἂν ἐπιτηδεύσειεν ἐφιλονείκει τὴν τῶν ἤδη γεγενημένων ἐπίδειξιν ὑπερβαλέσθαι, καί φασιν αὐτόν τε Καίσαρα καὶ Ἀγρίππαν πολλάκις εἰπεῖν, ὡς ἀποδέοι τὰ τῆς ἀρχῆς Ἡρώδῃ τῆς οὔσης ἐν αὐτῷ μεγαλοψυχίας: ἄξιον γὰρ εἶναι καὶ Συρίας ἁπάσης καὶ Αἰγύπτου τὴν βασιλείαν ἔχειν.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num142" xml:id="greek-book16-num142" id="greek-book16-num142" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> Μετὰ δὲ τὴν πανήγυριν ταύτην καὶ τὰς ἑορτὰς πόλιν ἄλλην ἀνήγειρεν ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ τῷ λεγομένῳ Καφαρσαβᾶ τόπον ἔνυδρον καὶ χώραν ἀρίστην φυτοῖς ἐκλέξας, ποταμοῦ τε περιρρέοντος τὴν πόλιν αὐτὴν καὶ καλλίστου κατὰ μέγεθος τῶν φυτῶν περιειληφότος ἄλσους.  ταύτην ἀπὸ Ἀντιπάτρου τοῦ πατρὸς Ἀντιπατρίδα προσηγόρευσεν. ἐπώνυμον δὲ καὶ τῇ μητρὶ χωρίον ὑπὲρ Ἱεριχοῦν οἰκοδομήσας ἀσφαλείᾳ τε διάφορον καὶ καταγωγαῖς ἥδιστον ἐκάλεσεν Κύπρον.  Φασαήλῳ τε τῷ ἀδελφῷ μνημεῖα διὰ τὴν γεγενημένην εἰς αὐτὸν φιλοστοργίαν ἀνετίθει τὰ κάλλιστα, πύργον ἐπ᾽ αὐτῆς τῆς πόλεως ἀναστήσας οὐδὲν ἐλάττω τοῦ κατὰ τὴν Φάρον, ὃν προσηγόρευσεν Φασάηλον, ἀσφαλείας τε τῇ πόλει μέρος ὄντα καὶ μνήμης τῷ τετελευτηκότι διὰ τὴν προσηγορίαν.  ὁμώνυμον δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ πόλιν περὶ τὸν αὐλῶνα τῆς Ἱεριχοῦντος ἔκτισεν ἀπιόντων κατὰ βορρᾶν ἄνεμον, δι᾽ ἧς καὶ τὴν πέριξ χώραν ἔρημον οὖσαν ἐνεργοτέραν ἐποίησεν ταῖς ἐπιμελείαις τῶν οἰκητόρων. Φασαηλίδα καὶ ταύτην ἐκάλει.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num146" xml:id="greek-book16-num146" id="greek-book16-num146" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> Τὰς δὲ ἄλλας εὐεργεσίας ἄπορον εἰπεῖν ὅσας ἀπέδωκεν ταῖς πόλεσιν ἔν τε Συρίᾳ καὶ κατὰ τὴν Ἑλλάδα καὶ παρ᾽ οἷς ποτ᾽ ἂν ἀποδημήσας τύχοι: καὶ γὰρ πλείους λειτουργίας καὶ δημοσίων ἔργων κατασκευὰς καὶ χρήματα τοῖς δεομένοις ἔργοις εἰς ἐπιμέλειαν τῶν προτέρων ἔργων ἐκλελοιπότων ἄφθονα χαρίσασθαι δοκεῖ.  τὰ δὲ μέγιστα καὶ διασημότατα τῶν πεπραγμένων αὐτῷ Ῥοδίοις μὲν τό τε Πύθιον ἀνέστησεν οἰκείοις ἀναλώμασιν καὶ παρέσχεν ἀργυρίου πολλὰ τάλαντα πρὸς ναυπηγίαν. Νικοπολίταις δὲ τοῖς ἐπ᾽ Ἀκτίῳ κτισθεῖσιν ὑπὸ Καίσαρος τὰ πλεῖστα τῶν δημοσίων συγκατεσκεύασεν.  Ἀντιοχεῦσι δὲ τοῖς ἐν Συρίᾳ μεγίστην πόλιν οἰκοῦσιν, ἣν κατὰ μῆκος τέμνει πλατεῖα, ταύτην αὐτὴν στοαῖς παρ᾽ ἑκάτερα καὶ λίθῳ τὴν ὕπαιθρον ὁδὸν ξεστῷ καταστορέσας πλεῖστον εἰς κόσμον καὶ τὴν τῶν οἰκούντων εὐχρηστίαν ὠφέλησεν.  τόν γε μὴν Ὀλυμπίασιν ἀγῶνα πολὺ τῆς προσηγορίας ἀδοξότερον ὑπ᾽ ἀχρηματίας διατεθειμένον τιμιώτερον ἐποίει χρημάτων προσόδους καταστήσας καὶ πρὸς θυσίας καὶ τὸν ἄλλον κόσμον ἐσεμνοποίησεν τὴν πανήγυριν. διὰ δὴ ταύτην τὴν φιλοτιμίαν διηνεκὴς ἀγωνοθέτης παρὰ τοῖς Ἠλείοις ἀνεγράφη.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num150" xml:id="greek-book16-num150" id="greek-book16-num150" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> Τοῖς μὲν οὖν ἄλλοις ἐπέρχεται θαυμάζειν τὸ διεστὸς τῆς ἐν τῇ φύσει προαιρέσεως: ὅταν μὲν γὰρ εἰς τὰς φιλοτιμίας καὶ τὰς εὐεργεσίας ἀπίδωμεν, αἷς ἐκέχρητο πρὸς ἅπαντας ἀνθρώπους, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅπως οὐκ ἄν τις αὐτὸν καὶ τῶν ἔλαττον τετιμημένων ἠρνήθη μὴ συνομολογεῖν εὐεργετικωτάτῃ κεχρῆσθαι τῇ φύσει.  ὅταν δὲ εἰς τὰς τιμωρίας καὶ ἀδικίας, ἃς εἰς τοὺς ἀρχομένους καὶ τοὺς οἰκειοτάτους ἐπεδείξατο βλέψῃ καὶ καταμάθῃ τὸ σκληρὸν καὶ τὸ δυσπαράκλητον τοῦ τρόπου, νικηθήσεται θηριώδη δοκεῖν καὶ πάσης μετριότητος ἀλλότριον.  ἔνθεν καὶ διάφορόν τινα καὶ μαχομένην ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ νομίζουσιν γενέσθαι τὴν προαίρεσιν. ἐγὼ δ᾽ οὐχ οὕτως ἔχων μίαν αἰτίαν ἀμφοτέρων τούτων ὑπολαμβάνω:  φιλότιμος γὰρ ὢν καὶ τούτου τοῦ πάθους ἡττημένος ἰσχυρῶς, προήγετο μὲν εἰς μεγαλοψυχίαν, εἴ που μνήμης εἰς αὖθις ἢ κατὰ τὸ παρὸν εὐφημίας ἐλπὶς ἐμπέσοι.  ταῖς δὲ δαπάναις ὑπὲρ δύναμιν χρώμενος ἠναγκάζετο χαλεπὸς εἶναι τοῖς ὑποτεταγμένοις: τὰ γὰρ εἰς οὓς ἐδαπάνα πολλὰ γενόμενα κακῶν ποριστὴν ἐξ ὧν ἐλάμβανεν ἐποίει.  καὶ συνειδὼς ἐφ᾽ οἷς ἠδίκει τοὺς ὑποτεταγμένους μισούμενον ἑαυτὸν τὸ μὲν ἐπανορθοῦσθαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας οὐ ῥᾴδιον ἐνόμιζεν: οὐδὲ γὰρ εἰς τὰς προσόδους λυσιτελὲς ἦν. ἀντεφιλονείκει δὲ τὴν δύσνοιαν αὐτὴν εὐπορίας ἀφορμὴν ποιούμενος.  περί γε μὴν τοὺς οἰκείους, εἴ τις ἢ λόγῳ μὴ θεραπεύοι τὸ δοῦλον ἐξομολογούμενος ἢ δόξειεν εἰς τὴν ἀρχήν τι παρακινεῖν, οὐχ ἱκανὸς ἑαυτοῦ κρατεῖν ἐγίνετο καὶ διεξῆλθεν ὁμοῦ συγγενεῖς καὶ φίλους ἴσα πολεμίοις τιμωρούμενος ἐκ τοῦ μόνος ἐθέλειν τετιμῆσθαι τὰς τοιαύτας ἁμαρτίας ἀναλαμβάνων.  μαρτύριον δέ μοι τούτου τοῦ πάθους, ὅτι μέγιστον περὶ αὐτὸν ἦν, καὶ τὰ γινόμενα κατὰ τὰς Καίσαρος καὶ Ἀγρίππα καὶ τῶν ἄλλων φίλων τιμάς: οἷς γὰρ ἐθεράπευεν τοὺς κρείττονας, τούτοις καὶ αὐτὸς ἠξίου θεραπεύεσθαι καὶ τὸ κάλλιστον ὧν ᾤετο παρέχων ἐν τῷ διδόναι τὴν τοῦ τυχεῖν τῶν ὁμοίων ἐπιθυμίαν ἐδήλου.  τό γε μὴν Ἰουδαίων ἔθνος ἠλλοτρίωται νόμῳ πρὸς πάντα τὰ τοιαῦτα καὶ συνείθισται τὸ δίκαιον ἀντὶ τοῦ πρὸς δόξαν ἠγαπηκέναι. διόπερ οὐκ ἦν αὐτῷ κεχαρισμένον, ὅτι μὴ δυνατὸν εἰκόσιν ἢ ναοῖς ἢ τοιούτοις ἐπιτηδεύμασιν κολακεύειν τοῦ βασιλέως τὸ φιλότιμον.  αἰτία μὲν αὕτη μοι δοκεῖ τῆς Ἡρώδου περὶ μὲν τοὺς οἰκείους καὶ συμβούλους ἁμαρτίας, περὶ δὲ τοὺς ἔξω καὶ μὴ προσήκοντας εὐεργεσίας.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>

chapters.Latin:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-5-1" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="136"><tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num136" id="latin-book16-num136" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="10" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" hidden="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone>X. Eodem tempore perfecta est caesarea quam edificauit decemnali tempore uicesimo octauo anno regni sui. Olimpiade centesima et nonagesima secunda, cuius in dedicatione caelebratio uel apparatus muni ficentissimus fuit. Nam praeceperat certamina musica uel palestras conuenire, praeparauerat etiam feras uel gladiatores cursusque equorum et reliqua miranda spectacula in honorem quinquennalis caesaris. Cui cum sua uxore iulia pro dedicatione ciuitatis maxima liberalitate summum ei derexerat apparatum, quorum summa quingentis talentis aestimata est. Cumque multitudo ad ciuitatem conuennisset pro spectaculis et legationes quas populi destinauerant beneficus eius gratias agentes pariter occurrissent. Cunctos suscepit in diuersoriis et conuiis per dies quindecim spectacula uel delicias ministrauit. Vnde insignis eius magnanimitas potuit diuulgari. Qua propter prohibent cesarem uel agrippam saepius dixisse, quod magnanimitate herodis imperium eius deesset, et dignum eum esse, syriae uel aegypti regnum possidere.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.English:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-5-1" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="136"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num136" xml:id="english-book16-num136" id="english-book16-num136" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="10" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" hidden="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[136]</tei-num> ABOUT this time it was that Cesarea Sebaste, which he had built, was finished. The entire building being accomplished: in the tenth year, the solemnity of it fell into the twenty-eighth year of Herod's reign, and into the hundred and ninety-second olympiad. There was accordingly a great festival and most sumptuous preparations made presently, in order to its dedication; for he had appointed a contention in music, and games to be performed naked. He had also gotten ready a great number of those that fight single combats, and of beasts for the like purpose; horse races also, and the most chargeable of such sports and shows as used to be exhibited at Rome, and in other places. He consecrated this combat to Caesar, and ordered it to be celebrated every fifth year. He also sent all sorts of ornaments for it out of his own furniture, that it might want nothing to make it decent; nay, Julia, Caesar's wife, sent a great part of her most valuable furniture [from Rome], insomuch that he had no want of any thing. The sum of them all was estimated at five hundred talents. Now when a great multitude was come to that city to see the shows, as well as the ambassadors whom other people sent, on account of the benefits they had received from Herod, he entertained them all in the public inns, and at public tables, and with perpetual feasts; this solemnity having in the day time the diversions of the fights, and in the night time such merry meetings as cost vast sums of money, and publicly demonstrated the generosity of his soul; for in all his undertakings he was ambitious to exhibit what exceeded whatsoever had been done before of the same kind. And it is related that Caesar and Agrippa often said, that the dominions of Herod were too little for the greatness of his soul; for that he deserved to have both all the kingdom of Syria, and that of Egypt also.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>

<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-5-1" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="136"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num136" xml:id="greek-book16-num136" id="greek-book16-num136" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="10" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" hidden="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone> Περὶ δὲ τὸν χρόνον τοῦτον συντέλειαν ἔλαβεν ἡ Καισάρεια Σεβαστή, ἣν ᾠκοδόμει δεκάτῳ μὲν ἔτει πρὸς τέλος ἐλθούσης αὐτῷ τῆς ὅλης κατασκευῆς, ἐκπεσούσης δὲ τῆς προθεσμίας εἰς ὄγδοον καὶ εἰκοστὸν ἔτος τῆς ἀρχῆς ἐπ᾽ ὀλυμπιάδος δευτέρας καὶ ἐνενηκοστῆς πρὸς ταῖς ἑκατόν.  ἦν οὖν εὐθὺς ἐν καθιερώσει μείζονες ἑορταὶ καὶ παρασκευαὶ πολυτελέσταται: κατηγγέλκει μὲν γὰρ ἀγῶνα μουσικῆς καὶ γυμνικῶν ἀθλημάτων, παρεσκευάκει δὲ πολὺ πλῆθος μονομάχων καὶ θηρίων ἵππων τε δρόμον καὶ τὰ πολυτελέστερα τῶν ἔν τε τῇ Ῥώμῃ καὶ παρ᾽ ἄλλοις τισὶν ἐπιτηδευμάτων.  ἀνετίθει δὲ καὶ τοῦτον τὸν ἀγῶνα Καίσαρι κατὰ πενταετηρίδα παρεσκευασμένος ἄγειν αὐτόν: ὁ δ᾽ αὐτῷ πᾶσαν τὴν εἰς τὰ τοιαῦτα παρασκευὴν ἀπὸ τῶν οἰκείων διεπέμπετο τὴν φιλοτιμίαν ἐπικοσμῶν.  ἰδίᾳ δὲ καὶ ἡ γυνὴ Καίσαρος Ἰουλία πολλὰ τῶν ἐκεῖ πολυτελεστάτων ἀπέστειλεν, ὡς μηδὲν ὑστερεῖν τὰ πάντα συντιμώμενα ταλάντων πεντακοσίων.  συνελθόντος δ᾽ εἰς τὴν πόλιν ὄχλου πλείονος κατὰ θεωρίαν καὶ πρεσβείας, ἃς ἔπεμπον οἱ δῆμοι δι᾽ ἃς ἐπεπόνθεισαν εὐεργεσίας, ἅπαντας ἐξεδέξατο καὶ καταγωγαῖς καὶ τραπέζαις καὶ διηνεκέσιν ἑορταῖς, τῆς πανηγύρεως ἐν μὲν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐχούσης τὰς ἀπὸ τῶν θεαμάτων ψυχαγωγίας, ἐν δὲ ταῖς νυξὶ τὰς εὐφροσύνας καὶ τὴν εἰς τοῦτο πολυτέλειαν, ὡς ἐπίσημον γενέσθαι τὴν μεγαλοψυχίαν αὐτοῦ:  εἰς πάντα γὰρ ἅπερ ἂν ἐπιτηδεύσειεν ἐφιλονείκει τὴν τῶν ἤδη γεγενημένων ἐπίδειξιν ὑπερβαλέσθαι, καί φασιν αὐτόν τε Καίσαρα καὶ Ἀγρίππαν πολλάκις εἰπεῖν, ὡς ἀποδέοι τὰ τῆς ἀρχῆς Ἡρώδῃ τῆς οὔσης ἐν αὐτῷ μεγαλοψυχίας: ἄξιον γὰρ εἶναι καὶ Συρίας ἁπάσης καὶ Αἰγύπτου τὴν βασιλείαν ἔχειν.</tei-p>

chapters.Latin:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-5-2" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="142"><tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num142" id="latin-book16-num142" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Post huius urbis dedicationem in campo qui cafarsaba uocabatur. Loco aquoso et terra optima arboribus, et fluuio circumdata ciuitatem aedificauit. Quam nomine antipatridam nuncupauit pulcritudine uel amoenitate decoratam Nec non et in nomine matris locum iuxta hierichuntem aedificans munitionem uel domiciliis optimum cyprum nomina <tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00396.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="196v" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>uit. Immo et in nomine fratris falsa eli propter amorem quem in eum habuerat construxit turrem in ea ciuitate non minorem faro alexandrino promonitione ciuitatis, quem in fratris memoriam fasaheleum uocauit. Apellationis uero eiusdem et ciuitatem circa hierichuntem condidit.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.English:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-5-2" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="142"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num142" xml:id="english-book16-num142" id="english-book16-num142" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[142]</tei-num> After this solemnity and these festivals were over, Herod erected another city in the plain called Capharsaba, where he chose out a fit place, both for plenty of water and goodness of soil, and proper for the production of what was there planted, where a river encompassed the city itself, and a grove of the best trees for magnitude was round about it: this he named Antipatris, from his father Antipater. He also built upon another spot of ground above Jericho, of the same name with his mother, a place of great security and very pleasant for habitation, and called it Cypros. He also dedicated the finest monuments to his brother Phasaelus, on account of the great natural affection there had been between them, by erecting a tower in the city itself, not less than the tower of Pharos, which he named Phasaelus, which was at once a part of the strong defenses of the city, and a memorial for him that was deceased, because it bare his name. He also built a city of the same name in the valley of Jericho, as you go from it northward, whereby he rendered the neighboring country more fruitful by the cultivation its inhabitants introduced; and this also he called Phasaelus.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.Greek:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-5-2" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="142"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num142" xml:id="greek-book16-num142" id="greek-book16-num142" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> Μετὰ δὲ τὴν πανήγυριν ταύτην καὶ τὰς ἑορτὰς πόλιν ἄλλην ἀνήγειρεν ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ τῷ λεγομένῳ Καφαρσαβᾶ τόπον ἔνυδρον καὶ χώραν ἀρίστην φυτοῖς ἐκλέξας, ποταμοῦ τε περιρρέοντος τὴν πόλιν αὐτὴν καὶ καλλίστου κατὰ μέγεθος τῶν φυτῶν περιειληφότος ἄλσους.  ταύτην ἀπὸ Ἀντιπάτρου τοῦ πατρὸς Ἀντιπατρίδα προσηγόρευσεν. ἐπώνυμον δὲ καὶ τῇ μητρὶ χωρίον ὑπὲρ Ἱεριχοῦν οἰκοδομήσας ἀσφαλείᾳ τε διάφορον καὶ καταγωγαῖς ἥδιστον ἐκάλεσεν Κύπρον.  Φασαήλῳ τε τῷ ἀδελφῷ μνημεῖα διὰ τὴν γεγενημένην εἰς αὐτὸν φιλοστοργίαν ἀνετίθει τὰ κάλλιστα, πύργον ἐπ᾽ αὐτῆς τῆς πόλεως ἀναστήσας οὐδὲν ἐλάττω τοῦ κατὰ τὴν Φάρον, ὃν προσηγόρευσεν Φασάηλον, ἀσφαλείας τε τῇ πόλει μέρος ὄντα καὶ μνήμης τῷ τετελευτηκότι διὰ τὴν προσηγορίαν.  ὁμώνυμον δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ πόλιν περὶ τὸν αὐλῶνα τῆς Ἱεριχοῦντος ἔκτισεν ἀπιόντων κατὰ βορρᾶν ἄνεμον, δι᾽ ἧς καὶ τὴν πέριξ χώραν ἔρημον οὖσαν ἐνεργοτέραν ἐποίησεν ταῖς ἐπιμελείαις τῶν οἰκητόρων. Φασαηλίδα καὶ ταύτην ἐκάλει.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>

chapters.Latin:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-5-3" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="146"><tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num146" id="latin-book16-num146" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Beneficia uero ipsius quae aliis ciuitatibus per syriam et ela da uel apud quos contigit perficisci donauit minime possumus explanare, nobilissima uero uel maxima facta eius in rodios extiterunt. Siquidem pithium ipse suis sumptibus contruxit, et praebuit multa talenta ad nauium confectiones, in ni copolitana etiam ciuitate quam in accio caesar aedificauerat multa publica loca condidit antiochenis uero magnam ciuitatem syriae habitantibus plateam longam in media ciuitate positam. Ex utraque parte porticibus ordinauit et uiam lapide polito strauit, ad hornatum et uoluptate habitantium nec non et olimpia cum certamen appellatione dignum propter pecuniarum inopiam melius reditibus deputatis refecit, et immolationibus uel reliquo ornatu caelebrationem eius insignem reddidit. Pro qua munificentia per petuus agonotheta nominatus est,</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.English:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-5-3" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="146"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num146" xml:id="english-book16-num146" id="english-book16-num146" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[146]</tei-num> But as for his other benefits, it is impossible to reckon them up, those which he bestowed on cities, both in Syria and in Greece, and in all the places he came to in his voyages; for he seems to have conferred, and that after a most plentiful manner, what would minister to many necessities, and the building of public works, and gave them the money that was necessary to such works as wanted it, to support them upon the failure of their other revenues: but what was the greatest and most illustrious of all his works, he erected Apollo's temple at Rhodes, at his own expenses, and gave them a great number of talents of silver for the repair of their fleet. He also built the greatest part of the public edifices for the inhabitants of Nicopolis, at Actium; and for the Antiochinus, the inhabitants of the principal city of Syria, where a broad street cuts through the place lengthways, he built cloisters along it on both sides, and laid the open road with polished stone, and was of very great advantage to the inhabitants. And as to the olympic games, which were in a very low condition, by reason of the failure of their revenues, he recovered their reputation, and appointed revenues for heir maintenance, and made that solemn meeting more venerable, as to the sacrifices and other ornaments; and by reason of this vast liberality, he was generally declared in their inscriptions to be one of the perpetual managers of those games.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.Greek:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-5-3" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="146"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num146" xml:id="greek-book16-num146" id="greek-book16-num146" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> Τὰς δὲ ἄλλας εὐεργεσίας ἄπορον εἰπεῖν ὅσας ἀπέδωκεν ταῖς πόλεσιν ἔν τε Συρίᾳ καὶ κατὰ τὴν Ἑλλάδα καὶ παρ᾽ οἷς ποτ᾽ ἂν ἀποδημήσας τύχοι: καὶ γὰρ πλείους λειτουργίας καὶ δημοσίων ἔργων κατασκευὰς καὶ χρήματα τοῖς δεομένοις ἔργοις εἰς ἐπιμέλειαν τῶν προτέρων ἔργων ἐκλελοιπότων ἄφθονα χαρίσασθαι δοκεῖ.  τὰ δὲ μέγιστα καὶ διασημότατα τῶν πεπραγμένων αὐτῷ Ῥοδίοις μὲν τό τε Πύθιον ἀνέστησεν οἰκείοις ἀναλώμασιν καὶ παρέσχεν ἀργυρίου πολλὰ τάλαντα πρὸς ναυπηγίαν. Νικοπολίταις δὲ τοῖς ἐπ᾽ Ἀκτίῳ κτισθεῖσιν ὑπὸ Καίσαρος τὰ πλεῖστα τῶν δημοσίων συγκατεσκεύασεν.  Ἀντιοχεῦσι δὲ τοῖς ἐν Συρίᾳ μεγίστην πόλιν οἰκοῦσιν, ἣν κατὰ μῆκος τέμνει πλατεῖα, ταύτην αὐτὴν στοαῖς παρ᾽ ἑκάτερα καὶ λίθῳ τὴν ὕπαιθρον ὁδὸν ξεστῷ καταστορέσας πλεῖστον εἰς κόσμον καὶ τὴν τῶν οἰκούντων εὐχρηστίαν ὠφέλησεν.  τόν γε μὴν Ὀλυμπίασιν ἀγῶνα πολὺ τῆς προσηγορίας ἀδοξότερον ὑπ᾽ ἀχρηματίας διατεθειμένον τιμιώτερον ἐποίει χρημάτων προσόδους καταστήσας καὶ πρὸς θυσίας καὶ τὸν ἄλλον κόσμον ἐσεμνοποίησεν τὴν πανήγυριν. διὰ δὴ ταύτην τὴν φιλοτιμίαν διηνεκὴς ἀγωνοθέτης παρὰ τοῖς Ἠλείοις ἀνεγράφη.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>

chapters.Latin:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-5-4" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="150"><tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num150" id="latin-book16-num150" data-origname="p" data-processed="">aliis quidem mira uidetur differentia uoluntatis naturae eius. Nam si largitiones considerentur quae omnibus donauit hominibus quis potest negare munificentissimae naturae eum fuisse. Si uero tormenta et iniquitates in subiectos uel domesticos eius adtendantur dirissimus et ferus omnique pietate alienus putatur. Vnde inconstantem et sibi contrariam uoluntatem eius existimant. Quod ego minime puto dum unam causam in utroque dominante considero nam dum ad in mensa largitionem munificentiam produceretur. Si alicubi praesentis gloriae spes occurrisset uel futurae sumptibus profusis alacriter eam emere<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb> festinabat. Qua propter conpellebatur seuus in subiectos existere. Dum praesentibus cunsumptis pecuniis alias uellet adquirere. Cumque cognosceret propter uiolentias suas se subiectorum odio teneri corrigere quidem uitia non facile poterat conabatur autem odium suum occasione pecuniarum ulcisci. Ea miliarum uero qui eum uerbo non placasset se seruum dicendo aut si suspicatus fuisset aliquem de principatu cogitare, nullatenus se poterat moderari sed persequebatur et cognatos et amicos taquam hostes, et dum uellet solum se honorari talibus delictis subcubuit. Testimonium autem nihil prebent huius modi passionis eum fuisse in caesarem uel agrippam uel in alios amicos honores exibiti. Nam qualiter ipse adulabatur maioribus similiter sibi fieri as subditis expetebat. Sed gens iudaeorum lege hoc agere prohibetur et contempta nagila solam expectat iustitiam. Vnde rex eos exosos habebat quod non potuissent eum templis uel imaginibus onorare huius rei gratia arbitror herodem in suos quidem feuissimum, in extraneos uero munificum paruisse.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.English:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-5-4" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="150"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num150" xml:id="english-book16-num150" id="english-book16-num150" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[150]</tei-num> Now some there are who stand amazed at the diversity of Herod's nature and purposes; for when we have respect to his magnificence, and the benefits which he bestowed on all mankind, there is no possibility for even those that had the least respect for him to deny, or not openly to confess, that he had a nature vastly beneficent; but when any one looks upon the punishments he inflicted, and the injuries he did, not only to his subjects, but to his nearest relations, and takes notice of his severe and unrelenting disposition there, he will be forced to allow that he was brutish, and a stranger to all humanity; insomuch that these men suppose his nature to be different, and sometimes at contradiction with itself; but I am myself of another opinion, and imagine that the occasion of both these sort of actions was one and the same; for being a man ambitious of honor, and quite overcome by that passion, he was induced to be magnificent, wherever there appeared any hopes of a future memorial, or of reputation at present; and as his expenses were beyond his abilities, he was necessitated to be harsh to his subjects; for the persons on whom he expended his money were so many, that they made him a very bad procurer of it; and because he was conscious that he was hated by those under him, for the injuries he did them, he thought it not an easy thing to amend his offenses, for that it was inconvenient for his revenue; he therefore strove on the other side to make their ill-will an occasion of his gains. As to his own court, therefore, if any one was not very obsequious to him in his language, and would not confess himself to be his slave, or but seemed to think of any innovation in his government, he was not able to contain himself, but prosecuted his very kindred and friends, and punished them as if they were enemies and this wickedness he undertook out of a desire that he might be himself alone honored. Now for this, my assertion about that passion of his, we have the greatest evidence, by what he did to honor Caesar and Agrippa, and his other friends; for with what honors he paid his respects to them who were his superiors, the same did he desire to be paid to himself; and what he thought the most excellent present he could make another, he discovered an inclination to have the like presented to himself. But now the Jewish nation is by their law a stranger to all such things, and accustomed to prefer righteousness to glory; for which reason that nation was not agreeable to him, because it was out of their power to flatter the king's ambition with statues or temples, or any other such performances; And this seems to me to have been at once the occasion of Herod's crimes as to his own courtiers and counselors, and of his benefactions as to foreigners and those that had no relation to him.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.Greek:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-5-4" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="150"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num150" xml:id="greek-book16-num150" id="greek-book16-num150" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> Τοῖς μὲν οὖν ἄλλοις ἐπέρχεται θαυμάζειν τὸ διεστὸς τῆς ἐν τῇ φύσει προαιρέσεως: ὅταν μὲν γὰρ εἰς τὰς φιλοτιμίας καὶ τὰς εὐεργεσίας ἀπίδωμεν, αἷς ἐκέχρητο πρὸς ἅπαντας ἀνθρώπους, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅπως οὐκ ἄν τις αὐτὸν καὶ τῶν ἔλαττον τετιμημένων ἠρνήθη μὴ συνομολογεῖν εὐεργετικωτάτῃ κεχρῆσθαι τῇ φύσει.  ὅταν δὲ εἰς τὰς τιμωρίας καὶ ἀδικίας, ἃς εἰς τοὺς ἀρχομένους καὶ τοὺς οἰκειοτάτους ἐπεδείξατο βλέψῃ καὶ καταμάθῃ τὸ σκληρὸν καὶ τὸ δυσπαράκλητον τοῦ τρόπου, νικηθήσεται θηριώδη δοκεῖν καὶ πάσης μετριότητος ἀλλότριον.  ἔνθεν καὶ διάφορόν τινα καὶ μαχομένην ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ νομίζουσιν γενέσθαι τὴν προαίρεσιν. ἐγὼ δ᾽ οὐχ οὕτως ἔχων μίαν αἰτίαν ἀμφοτέρων τούτων ὑπολαμβάνω:  φιλότιμος γὰρ ὢν καὶ τούτου τοῦ πάθους ἡττημένος ἰσχυρῶς, προήγετο μὲν εἰς μεγαλοψυχίαν, εἴ που μνήμης εἰς αὖθις ἢ κατὰ τὸ παρὸν εὐφημίας ἐλπὶς ἐμπέσοι.  ταῖς δὲ δαπάναις ὑπὲρ δύναμιν χρώμενος ἠναγκάζετο χαλεπὸς εἶναι τοῖς ὑποτεταγμένοις: τὰ γὰρ εἰς οὓς ἐδαπάνα πολλὰ γενόμενα κακῶν ποριστὴν ἐξ ὧν ἐλάμβανεν ἐποίει.  καὶ συνειδὼς ἐφ᾽ οἷς ἠδίκει τοὺς ὑποτεταγμένους μισούμενον ἑαυτὸν τὸ μὲν ἐπανορθοῦσθαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας οὐ ῥᾴδιον ἐνόμιζεν: οὐδὲ γὰρ εἰς τὰς προσόδους λυσιτελὲς ἦν. ἀντεφιλονείκει δὲ τὴν δύσνοιαν αὐτὴν εὐπορίας ἀφορμὴν ποιούμενος.  περί γε μὴν τοὺς οἰκείους, εἴ τις ἢ λόγῳ μὴ θεραπεύοι τὸ δοῦλον ἐξομολογούμενος ἢ δόξειεν εἰς τὴν ἀρχήν τι παρακινεῖν, οὐχ ἱκανὸς ἑαυτοῦ κρατεῖν ἐγίνετο καὶ διεξῆλθεν ὁμοῦ συγγενεῖς καὶ φίλους ἴσα πολεμίοις τιμωρούμενος ἐκ τοῦ μόνος ἐθέλειν τετιμῆσθαι τὰς τοιαύτας ἁμαρτίας ἀναλαμβάνων.  μαρτύριον δέ μοι τούτου τοῦ πάθους, ὅτι μέγιστον περὶ αὐτὸν ἦν, καὶ τὰ γινόμενα κατὰ τὰς Καίσαρος καὶ Ἀγρίππα καὶ τῶν ἄλλων φίλων τιμάς: οἷς γὰρ ἐθεράπευεν τοὺς κρείττονας, τούτοις καὶ αὐτὸς ἠξίου θεραπεύεσθαι καὶ τὸ κάλλιστον ὧν ᾤετο παρέχων ἐν τῷ διδόναι τὴν τοῦ τυχεῖν τῶν ὁμοίων ἐπιθυμίαν ἐδήλου.  τό γε μὴν Ἰουδαίων ἔθνος ἠλλοτρίωται νόμῳ πρὸς πάντα τὰ τοιαῦτα καὶ συνείθισται τὸ δίκαιον ἀντὶ τοῦ πρὸς δόξαν ἠγαπηκέναι. διόπερ οὐκ ἦν αὐτῷ κεχαρισμένον, ὅτι μὴ δυνατὸν εἰκόσιν ἢ ναοῖς ἢ τοιούτοις ἐπιτηδεύμασιν κολακεύειν τοῦ βασιλέως τὸ φιλότιμον.  αἰτία μὲν αὕτη μοι δοκεῖ τῆς Ἡρώδου περὶ μὲν τοὺς οἰκείους καὶ συμβούλους ἁμαρτίας, περὶ δὲ τοὺς ἔξω καὶ μὴ προσήκοντας εὐεργεσίας.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>

chapters.Latin:
<tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Chapter-6-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="160"><tei-div2 n="10" type="chapter" data-origname="div2" data-processed=""><tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num160" id="latin-book16-num160" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Interea iudaei per asyam et libiam atrociter affligebantur, dum non eisdem legibus sicut sub antiquis regibus uterentur sed uiolentia paganorum opprimerentur, ut pecunias sacras uiolenter amitterent. Ideoque ad caesarem pro his legationem destinauerunt, qui scribens per prouintiam suis eos legibus uti precepit quarum exempla subiunximus. Demonstrant enim uoluntatem quam ab initio pro nobis romani imperatores habuerunt</tei-p>
				</tei-div2>
				<tei-div2 n="11" type="chapter" data-origname="div2" data-processed="">
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num162" id="latin-book16-num162" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="11" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" hidden="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone>XI Caesar augustus pontifex tribunciae potestatis dicit. Quoniam gens iudeaorum fidelis non solum presenti tempore, sed etiam priori et magis patri meo dictatori caesari populoque romano et princeps eorum hyrcanus apparuit Placuit mihi et senatui cum sententia populi romani iudaeos suis legibus et patrio iure frui permittere. Sicut sub hyrcano <tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00397.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="197r" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb> principe sacerdotum altissimi dei et secra ria eorum inuiolata permarere, et pecunias ab eis ab hierosolimam transmissas reddi custodibus pecuniarum. Neque uadimonia sabbato uel sexto die ab hora non exigi. Siquis autem inuentus fuerit auferent sacros sanctos eorum codices aut pecunias a synagogis huiusmodi sacrilegio teneatur et substantia eius publico romae deputetur. Suggestionem uero eorum pro piaetate mea quam habeo super omnes homines per gaium martium censorinum mihi porrectam, et hoc decretum praecipio proponi in nobilissimo loco quem omnis asiam eo numini dedicauit. Siquis autem transgressus fuerit hanc constitutionem non mediocrem paenam exsoluet. Scriptum est in caesaris templo,</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num166" id="latin-book16-num166" data-origname="p" data-processed="">caesar norbano flacco salutem, iudaei qui antiquam consuetudinem solent pecunias sacras ad hierosolimam transmittere sine inpedimento hoc faciant, haec quidem caesar.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num167" id="latin-book16-num167" data-origname="p" data-processed="">agrippa uero scripsit per iudaeis hoc modo. Agrippe magistratibus senatui populoque phesiorum salutem. Pecuniarum sacrarumque in hierosolimorum templum transmittuntur, diligentiam et custodiam in asya iudaeos habere praecipio secundum patrium morem. Hos autem qui sacras pecunias iudaeorum auferunt et ad asilium confugiunt, iubeo de trai iudeisque tradi quod iure etiam sacrilegii detrahuntur. Scripsi uero silano magistratum gerenti ne sabbato iudaei conpellantur uadimonia prebere.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num169" id="latin-book16-num169" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Marcus agrippa quirinensium magistratibus senatui et populo salutem. Iudaei qui per cirenen quibus iam augustus scriptis in libia fabio magistratum gerenti aliisque ibi prouintiae procuratoribus quatenus sine inpedimento paecuniae hierosolimis secundum morem suum transmittantur. Nunc me interpellauerunt qui ab aliquibus<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb> calumpniatoribus affliguntur ocasione tributorum quae nequaquam debent et prohibentur solemnia sua per agere quo<tei-gap data-origname="gap" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-gap> nullo modo impediri admoneo. Sed et in quas sacras pecunias ciues ab eis abstulerunt has ipsis reddi praetio et in reliquo corrigi net alia committantur.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num171" id="latin-book16-num171" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Gaius norbanus flaccus proconsul sardiniensium magistratibus et senatui salutem. Caesar scripsit mihi praecipiens nequaquam iudaeos prohiberi patria consuetudine pecunias colligentes ad hierosolimam transmittere. Scripsi ergo uobis ut sciatis quem caesar et ego sic uolumus</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num172" id="latin-book16-num172" data-origname="p" data-processed="">nihilominus et iulius proconsul scripsit ita ephesiorum magistratibus senatui et populo salutem. Per asiam iudaei habitantes idibus <tei-expan data-origname="expan" data-processed="">februaris</tei-expan> ephesi mihi iudicanti demonstrauerunt caesarem augustum et agrippam concessisse eis propriis uti legibus immo et pri micias quas singuli eorum si uoluntate piaetatis causa quam in deo habent solent transmittere, habeant licentiam sine inpedimento hoc agere. Petierunt autem ut ego similiter cum decretis a caesare uel agrippa meam sententiam confirmarem. Volo igitur uos cognoscere quoniam decretis augustu et agrippae parens, praecipi eos uti et seruare sine inpedimento sua solemnia.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num174" id="latin-book16-num174" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Haec ideo explanauimus quoniam conscripta nostra amplius apud graecos uenturas ut demonstrem eis quia cunctum honorem ab initio impetrantes nihil ex patriis legibus prohibiti sumus a magistratibus agere sed et defendebamur religionem et honores in deo seruantes, quorum facio sepius mentionem ut mutatis <tei-expan data-origname="expan" data-processed="">saeculi</tei-expan> odiis causae quae nobis ob hoc uel illis inracionabiliter insertae sunt euellantur. Nam legibus hisdem nulla gens semper utitur dum et per ciuitates multa religionis differentia seruetur. Iustitia uero cunctis hominibus similiter studetur, quae commoda graecis uel barbaris existit, de qua nostrae leges multam rationem habentes omnes homines <tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00398.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="197v" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb> debent nos ut amicos et hospites amplecti, nam oportet non differentia nos religionum alienos facere, sed non seruatus benignitatis affectus, quae omnium hominum communem uitam poterit custodire redeo uero ad reliquam monumem ta conscriptionis.</tei-p>
				</tei-div2>
				<tei-div2 n="12" type="chapter" data-origname="div2" data-processed="">
					</tei-div2></tei-div>
chapters.English:
<tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Chapter-6-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="160"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num160" xml:id="english-book16-num160" id="english-book16-num160" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[160]</tei-num> Now the cities ill-treated the Jews in Asia, and all those also of the same nation which lived ill Libya, which joins to Cyrene, while the former kings had given them equal privileges with the other citizens; but the Greeks affronted them at this time, and that so far as to take away their sacred money, and to do them mischief on other particular occasions. When therefore they were thus afflicted, and found no end of their barbarous treatment they met with among the Greeks, they sent ambassadors to Caesar on those accounts, who gave them the same privileges as they had before, and sent letters to the same purpose to the governors of the provinces, copies of which I subjoin here, as testimonials of the ancient favorable disposition the Roman emperors had towards us.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num162" xml:id="english-book16-num162" id="english-book16-num162" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="11" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" hidden="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[162]</tei-num> "Caesar Augustus, high priest and tribune of the people, ordains thus: Since the nation of the Jews hath been found grateful to the Roman people, not only at this time, but in time past also, and chiefly Hyrcanus the high priest, under my father Caesar the emperor, it seemed good to me and my counselors, according to the sentence and oath of the people of Rome, that the Jews have liberty to make use of their own customs, according to the law of their forefathers, as they made use of them under Hyrcanus the high priest of the Almighty God; and that their sacred money be not touched, but be sent to Jerusalem, and that it be committed to the care of the receivers at Jerusalem; and that they be not obliged to go before any judge on the sabbath day, nor on the day of the preparation to it, after the ninth hour. But if any one be caught stealing their holy books, or their sacred money, whether it be out of the synagogue or public school, he shall be deemed a sacrilegious person, and his goods shall be brought into the public treasury of the Romans. And I give order that the testimonial which they have given me, on account of my regard to that piety which I exercise toward all mankind, and out of regard to Caius Marcus Censorinus, together with the present decree, be proposed in that most eminent place which hath been consecrated to me by the community of Asia at Ancyra. And if any one transgress any part of what is above decreed, he shall be severely punished." This was inscribed upon a pillar in the temple of Caesar.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num166" xml:id="english-book16-num166" id="english-book16-num166" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[166]</tei-num> "Caesar to Norbanus Flaccus, sendeth greeting. Let those Jews, how many soever they be, who have been used, according to their ancient custom, to send their sacred money to Jerusalem, do the same freely." These were the decrees of Caesar.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num167" xml:id="english-book16-num167" id="english-book16-num167" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[167]</tei-num> Agrippa also did himself write after the manner following, on behalf of the Jews: "Agrippa, to the magistrates, senate, and people of the Ephesians, sendeth greeting. I will that the care and custody of the sacred money that is carried to the temple at Jerusalem be left to the Jews of Asia, to do with it according to their ancient custom; and that such as steal that sacred money of the Jews, and fly to a sanctuary, shall be taken thence and delivered to the Jews, by the same law that sacrilegious persons are taken thence. I have also written to Sylvanus the praetor, that no one compel the Jews to come before a judge on the sabbath day."</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num169" xml:id="english-book16-num169" id="english-book16-num169" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[169]</tei-num> "Marcus Agrippa to the magistrates, senate, and people of Cyrene, sendeth greeting. The Jews of Cyrene have interceded with me for the performance of what Augustus sent orders about to Flavius, the then praetor of Libya, and to the other procurators of that province, that the sacred money may be sent to Jerusalem freely, as hath been their custom from their forefathers, they complaining that they are abused by certain informers, and under pretense of taxes which were not due, are hindered from sending them, which I command to be restored without any diminution or disturbance given to them. And if any of that sacred money in the cities be taken from their proper receivers, I further enjoin, that the same be exactly returned to the Jews in that place."</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num171" xml:id="english-book16-num171" id="english-book16-num171" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[171]</tei-num> "Caius Norbanus Flaccus, proconsul, to the magistrates of the Sardians, sendeth greeting. Caesar hath written to me, and commanded me not to forbid the Jews, how many soever they be, from assembling together according to the custom of their forefathers, nor from sending their money to Jerusalem. I have therefore written to you, that you may know that both Caesar and I would have you act accordingly."</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num172" xml:id="english-book16-num172" id="english-book16-num172" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[172]</tei-num> Nor did Julius Antonius, the proconsul, write otherwise. "To the magistrates, senate, and people of the Ephesians, sendeth greeting. As I was dispensing justice at Ephesus, on the Ides of February, the Jews that dwell in Asia demonstrated to me that Augustus and Agrippa had permitted them to use their own laws and customs, and to offer those their first-fruits, which every one of them freely offers to the Deity on account of piety, and to carry them in a company together to Jerusalem without disturbance. They also petitioned me that I also would confirm what had been granted by Augustus and Agrippa by my own sanction. I would therefore have you take notice, that according to the will of Augustus and Agrippa, I permit them to use and do according to the customs of their forefathers without disturbance."</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num174" xml:id="english-book16-num174" id="english-book16-num174" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[174]</tei-num> I have been obliged to set down these decree because the present history of our own acts will go generally among the Greeks; and I have hereby demonstrated to them that we have formerly been in great esteem, and have not been prohibited by those governors we were under from keeping any of the laws of our forefathers; nay, that we have been supported by them, while we followed our own religion, and the worship we paid to God; and I frequently make mention of these decrees, in order to reconcile other people to us, and to take away the causes of that hatred which unreasonable men bear to us. As for our customs there is no nation which always makes use of the same, and in every city almost we meet with them different from one another; but natural justice is most agreeable to the advantage of all men equally, both Greeks and barbarians, to which our laws have the greatest regard, and thereby render us, if we abide in them after a pure manner, benevolent and friendly to all men; on which account we have reason to expect the like return from others, and to inform them that they ought not to esteem difference of positive institutions a sufficient cause of alienation, but [join with us in] the pursuit of virtue and probity, for this belongs to all men in common, and of itself alone is sufficient for the preservation of human life. I now return to the thread of my history.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.Greek:
<tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Chapter-6-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="160"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num160" xml:id="greek-book16-num160" id="greek-book16-num160" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> Τοὺς δὲ κατὰ τὴν Ἀσίαν Ἰουδαίους καὶ ὅσους ἡ πρὸς Κυρήνῃ Λιβύη κατέσχεν ἐκάκουν αἱ πόλεις, τῶν μὲν πρότερον βασιλέων ἰσονομίαν αὐτοῖς παρεσχημένων, ἐν δὲ τῷ τότε δι᾽ ἐπηρείας ἐχόντων τῶν Ἑλλήνων αὐτούς, ὡς καὶ χρημάτων ἱερῶν ἀφαίρεσιν ποιεῖσθαι καὶ καταβλάπτειν ἐν τοῖς ἐπὶ μέρους.  πάσχοντες δὲ κακῶς καὶ πέρας οὐδὲν εὑρίσκοντες τῆς τῶν Ἑλλήνων ἀπανθρωπίας ἐπρεσβεύσαντο παρὰ Καίσαρα καὶ περὶ τούτων. ὁ δ᾽ αὐτοῖς τὴν αὐτὴν ἰσοτέλειαν ἔδωκεν γράψας τοῖς κατὰ τὰς ἐπαρχίας, ὧν ὑπετάξαμεν τὰ ἀντίγραφα μαρτύρια τῆς διαθέσεως, ἣν ἔσχον ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἄνωθεν οἱ κρατοῦντες.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num162" xml:id="greek-book16-num162" id="greek-book16-num162" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="11" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" hidden="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone> ‘Καῖσαρ Σεβαστὸς ἀρχιερεὺς δημαρχικῆς ἐξουσίας λέγει. ἐπειδὴ τὸ ἔθνος τὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων εὐχάριστον εὑρέθη οὐ μόνον ἐν τῷ ἐνεστῶτι καιρῷ ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τῷ προγεγενημένῳ καὶ μάλιστα ἐπὶ τοῦ ἐμοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοκράτορος Καίσαρος πρὸς τὸν δῆμον τὸν Ῥωμαίων ὅ τε ἀρχιερεὺς αὐτῶν Ὑρκανός,  ἔδοξέ μοι καὶ τῷ ἐμῷ συμβουλίῳ μετὰ ὁρκωμοσίας γνώμῃ δήμου Ῥωμαίων τοὺς Ἰουδαίους χρῆσθαι τοῖς ἰδίοις θεσμοῖς κατὰ τὸν πάτριον αὐτῶν νόμον, καθὼς ἐχρῶντο ἐπὶ Ὑρκανοῦ ἀρχιερέως θεοῦ ὑψίστου, τά τε ἱερὰ * εἶναι ἐν ἀσυλίᾳ καὶ ἀναπέμπεσθαι εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ ἀποδίδοσθαι τοῖς ἀποδοχεῦσιν Ἱεροσολύμων, ἐγγύας τε μὴ ὁμολογεῖν αὐτοὺς ἐν σάββασιν ἢ τῇ πρὸ αὐτῆς παρασκευῇ ἀπὸ ὥρας ἐνάτης.  ἐὰν δέ τις φωραθῇ κλέπτων τὰς ἱερὰς βίβλους αὐτῶν ἢ τὰ ἱερὰ χρήματα ἔκ τε σαββατείου ἔκ τε ἀνδρῶνος, εἶναι αὐτὸν ἱερόσυλον καὶ τὸν βίον αὐτοῦ ἐνεχθῆναι εἰς τὸ δημόσιον τῶν Ῥωμαίων.  τό τε ψήφισμα τὸ δοθέν μοι ὑπ᾽ αὐτῶν ὑπὲρ τῆς ἐμῆς εὐσεβείας ἧς ἔχω πρὸς πάντας ἀνθρώπους καὶ ὑπὲρ Γαΐου Μαρκίου Κηνσωρίνου καὶ τοῦτο τὸ διάταγμα κελεύω ἀνατεθῆναι ἐν ἐπισημοτάτῳ τόπῳ τῷ γενηθέντι μοι ὑπὸ τοῦ κοινοῦ τῆς Ἀσίας ἐν Ἀγκύρῃ. ἐὰν δέ τις παραβῇ τι τῶν προειρημένων, δώσει δίκην οὐ μετρίαν. ἐστηλογραφήθη ἐν τῷ Καίσαρος ναῷ.’</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num166" xml:id="greek-book16-num166" id="greek-book16-num166" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> ‘Καῖσαρ Νωρβανῷ Φλάκκῳ χαίρειν. Ἰουδαῖοι ὅσοι ποτ᾽ οὖν εἰσίν, οἳ δι᾽ ἀρχαίαν συνήθειαν εἰώθασιν χρήματά τε ἱερὰ φέροντες ἀναπέμπειν ἀκωλύτως τοῦτο ποιείτωσαν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.’ καὶ ταῦτα μὲν Καῖσαρ.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num167" xml:id="greek-book16-num167" id="greek-book16-num167" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> Ἀγρίππας δὲ καὶ αὐτὸς ἔγραψεν ὑπὲρ τῶν Ἰουδαίων τὸν τρόπον τοῦτον: ‘Ἀγρίππας Ἐφεσίων ἄρχουσι βουλῇ δήμῳ χαίρειν. τῶν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν τὸ ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἀναφερομένων ἱερῶν χρημάτων τὴν ἐπιμέλειαν καὶ φυλακὴν βούλομαι τοὺς ἐν Ἀσίᾳ Ἰουδαίους ποιεῖσθαι κατὰ τὰ πάτρια.  τούς τε κλέπτοντας ἱερὰ γράμματα τῶν Ἰουδαίων καταφεύγοντάς τε εἰς τὰς ἀσυλίας βούλομαι ἀποσπᾶσθαι καὶ παραδίδοσθαι τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις, ᾧ δικαίῳ ἀποσπῶνται οἱ ἱερόσυλοι. ἔγραψα δὲ καὶ Σιλανῷ τῷ στρατηγῷ, ἵνα σάββασιν μηδεὶς ἀναγκάζῃ Ἰουδαῖον ἐγγύας ὁμολογεῖν.’</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num169" xml:id="greek-book16-num169" id="greek-book16-num169" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> ‘Μᾶρκος Ἀγρίππας Κυρηναίων ἄρχουσιν βουλῇ δήμῳ χαίρειν. οἱ ἐν Κυρήνῃ Ἰουδαῖοι, ὑπὲρ ὧν ἤδη ὁ Σεβαστὸς ἔπεμψεν πρὸς τὸν ἐν Λιβύῃ στρατηγὸν τόντε ὄντα Φλάβιον καὶ πρὸς τοὺς ἄλλους τοὺς τῆς ἐπαρχίας ἐπιμελουμένους, ἵνα ἀνεπικωλύτως ἀναπέμπηται τὰ ἱερὰ χρήματα εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, ὡς ἔστιν αὐτοῖς πάτριον,  ἐνέτυχόν μοι νῦν, ὡς ὑπό τινων συκοφαντῶν ἐπηρεαζόμενοι καὶ ὡς ἐν προφάσει τελῶν μὴ ὀφειλομένων κωλύοιντο: οἷς ἀποκαθιστάνειν κατὰ μηδένα τρόπον ἐνοχλουμένοις, καὶ εἴ τινων ἱερὰ χρήματα ἀφῄρηνται τῶν πόλεων τοὺς εἰς ταῦτα ἀποκεκριμένους καὶ ταῦτα διορθώσασθαι τοῖς ἐκεῖ Ἰουδαίοις κελεύω.’</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num171" xml:id="greek-book16-num171" id="greek-book16-num171" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> ‘Γάιος Νωρβανὸς Φλάκκος ἀνθύπατος Σαρδιανῶν ἄρχουσι χαίρειν. Καῖσάρ μοι ἔγραψεν κελεύων μὴ κωλύεσθαι τοὺς Ἰουδαίους ὅσα ἂν ὦσιν κατὰ τὸ πάτριον αὐτοῖς ἔθος συναγαγόντες χρήματα ἀναπέμπειν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα. ἔγραψα οὖν ὑμῖν, ἵν᾽ εἰδῆτε, ὅτι Καῖσαρ κἀγὼ οὕτως θέλομεν γίνεσθαι.’</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num172" xml:id="greek-book16-num172" id="greek-book16-num172" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> Οὐδὲν ἧττον καὶ Ἰούλιος Ἀντώνιος ἀνθύπατος ἔγραψεν ‘Ἐφεσίων ἄρχουσιν βουλῇ δήμῳ χαίρειν. οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ κατοικοῦντες Ἰουδαῖοι εἰδοῖς Φεβρουαρίοις δικαιοδοτοῦντί μοι ἐν Ἐφέσῳ ὑπέδειξαν Καίσαρα τὸν Σεβαστὸν καὶ Ἀγρίππαν συγκεχωρηκέναι αὐτοῖς χρῆσθαι τοῖς ἰδίοις νόμοις καὶ ἔθεσιν, ἀπαρχάς τε, ἃς ἕκαστος αὐτῶν ἐκ τῆς ἰδίας προαιρέσεως εὐσεβείας ἕνεκα τῆς πρὸς τὸ θεῖον * ἀνακομιδῆς συμπορευομένους ποιεῖν ἀνεμποδίστως.  ᾔτουν τε, ὅπως κἀγὼ ὁμοίως τοῖς ὑπὸ τοῦ Σεβαστοῦ καὶ Ἀγρίππα δοθεῖσιν τὴν ἐμὴν γνώμην βεβαιώσω. ὑμᾶς οὖν βούλομαι εἰδέναι ἐν τοῖς τοῦ Σεβαστοῦ καὶ Ἀγρίππα βουλήμασιν συνεπιτρέπειν αὐτοῖς χρῆσθαι καὶ ποιεῖν κατὰ τὰ πάτρια χωρὶς ἐμποδισμοῦ.’</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num174" xml:id="greek-book16-num174" id="greek-book16-num174" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> Ταῦτα μὲν οὖν παρεθέμην ἐξ ἀνάγκης, ἐπειδὴ μέλλουσιν αἱ τῶν ἡμετέρων πράξεων ἀναγραφαὶ τὸ πλέον εἰς τοὺς Ἕλληνας ἰέναι, δεικνὺς αὐτοῖς ὅτι πάσης τιμῆς ἄνωθεν ἐπιτυγχάνοντες οὐδὲν τῶν πατρίων ἐκωλύθημεν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀρχόντων πράττειν, ἀλλὰ καὶ συνεργούμεθα τὰ τῆς θρησκείας ἔχοντες καὶ τῶν εἰς τὸν θεὸν τιμῶν.  ποιοῦμαι δὲ πολλάκις αὐτῶν τὴν μνήμην ἐπιδιαλλάττων τὰ γένη καὶ τὰς ἐμπεφυκυίας τοῖς ἀλογίστοις ἡμῶν τε κἀκείνων μίσους αἰτίας ὑπεξαιρούμενος.  ἔθεσιν μὲν γὰρ οὐδέν ἐστιν γένος ὃ τοῖς αὐτοῖς ἀεὶ χρῆται καὶ κατὰ πόλεις ἔσθ᾽ ὅπη πολλῆς ἐγγιγνομένης τῆς διαφορᾶς: τὸ δίκαιον δὲ πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις ὁμοίως ἐπιτηδεύοντες λυσιτελέστατον ὂν Ἕλλησίν τε καὶ βαρβάροις,  οὗ πλεῖστον οἱ παρ᾽ ἡμῖν νόμοι λόγον ἔχοντες ἅπασιν ἡμᾶς, εἰ καθαρῶς ἐμμένοιμεν αὐτοῖς, εὔνους καὶ φίλους ἀπεργάζονται.  διὸ καὶ ταῦτα παρ᾽ ἐκείνων ἡμῖν ἀπαιτητέον καὶ δέον οὐκ ἐν τῇ διαφορᾷ τῶν ἐπιτηδευμάτων οἴεσθαι τὸ ἀλλότριον, ἀλλ᾽ ἐν τῷ πρὸς καλοκαγαθίαν ἐπιτηδείως ἔχειν: τοῦτο γὰρ κοινὸν ἅπασιν καὶ μόνον ἱκανὸν διασώζειν τὸν τῶν ἀνθρώπων βίον. ἐπάνειμι δὲ πάλιν ἐπὶ τὰ συνεχῆ τῆς ἱστορίας.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>

chapters.Latin:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-1" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="160"><tei-div2 n="10" type="chapter" data-origname="div2" data-processed=""><tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num160" id="latin-book16-num160" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Interea iudaei per asyam et libiam atrociter affligebantur, dum non eisdem legibus sicut sub antiquis regibus uterentur sed uiolentia paganorum opprimerentur, ut pecunias sacras uiolenter amitterent. Ideoque ad caesarem pro his legationem destinauerunt, qui scribens per prouintiam suis eos legibus uti precepit quarum exempla subiunximus. Demonstrant enim uoluntatem quam ab initio pro nobis romani imperatores habuerunt</tei-p>
				</tei-div2>

chapters.Latin:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-2" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="162"><tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num162" id="latin-book16-num162" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="11" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" hidden="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone>XI Caesar augustus pontifex tribunciae potestatis dicit. Quoniam gens iudeaorum fidelis non solum presenti tempore, sed etiam priori et magis patri meo dictatori caesari populoque romano et princeps eorum hyrcanus apparuit Placuit mihi et senatui cum sententia populi romani iudaeos suis legibus et patrio iure frui permittere. Sicut sub hyrcano <tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00397.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="197r" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb> principe sacerdotum altissimi dei et secra ria eorum inuiolata permarere, et pecunias ab eis ab hierosolimam transmissas reddi custodibus pecuniarum. Neque uadimonia sabbato uel sexto die ab hora non exigi. Siquis autem inuentus fuerit auferent sacros sanctos eorum codices aut pecunias a synagogis huiusmodi sacrilegio teneatur et substantia eius publico romae deputetur. Suggestionem uero eorum pro piaetate mea quam habeo super omnes homines per gaium martium censorinum mihi porrectam, et hoc decretum praecipio proponi in nobilissimo loco quem omnis asiam eo numini dedicauit. Siquis autem transgressus fuerit hanc constitutionem non mediocrem paenam exsoluet. Scriptum est in caesaris templo,</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.English:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-2" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="162"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num162" xml:id="english-book16-num162" id="english-book16-num162" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="11" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" hidden="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[162]</tei-num> "Caesar Augustus, high priest and tribune of the people, ordains thus: Since the nation of the Jews hath been found grateful to the Roman people, not only at this time, but in time past also, and chiefly Hyrcanus the high priest, under my father Caesar the emperor, it seemed good to me and my counselors, according to the sentence and oath of the people of Rome, that the Jews have liberty to make use of their own customs, according to the law of their forefathers, as they made use of them under Hyrcanus the high priest of the Almighty God; and that their sacred money be not touched, but be sent to Jerusalem, and that it be committed to the care of the receivers at Jerusalem; and that they be not obliged to go before any judge on the sabbath day, nor on the day of the preparation to it, after the ninth hour. But if any one be caught stealing their holy books, or their sacred money, whether it be out of the synagogue or public school, he shall be deemed a sacrilegious person, and his goods shall be brought into the public treasury of the Romans. And I give order that the testimonial which they have given me, on account of my regard to that piety which I exercise toward all mankind, and out of regard to Caius Marcus Censorinus, together with the present decree, be proposed in that most eminent place which hath been consecrated to me by the community of Asia at Ancyra. And if any one transgress any part of what is above decreed, he shall be severely punished." This was inscribed upon a pillar in the temple of Caesar.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.Greek:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-2" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="162"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num162" xml:id="greek-book16-num162" id="greek-book16-num162" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="11" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" hidden="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone> ‘Καῖσαρ Σεβαστὸς ἀρχιερεὺς δημαρχικῆς ἐξουσίας λέγει. ἐπειδὴ τὸ ἔθνος τὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων εὐχάριστον εὑρέθη οὐ μόνον ἐν τῷ ἐνεστῶτι καιρῷ ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τῷ προγεγενημένῳ καὶ μάλιστα ἐπὶ τοῦ ἐμοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοκράτορος Καίσαρος πρὸς τὸν δῆμον τὸν Ῥωμαίων ὅ τε ἀρχιερεὺς αὐτῶν Ὑρκανός,  ἔδοξέ μοι καὶ τῷ ἐμῷ συμβουλίῳ μετὰ ὁρκωμοσίας γνώμῃ δήμου Ῥωμαίων τοὺς Ἰουδαίους χρῆσθαι τοῖς ἰδίοις θεσμοῖς κατὰ τὸν πάτριον αὐτῶν νόμον, καθὼς ἐχρῶντο ἐπὶ Ὑρκανοῦ ἀρχιερέως θεοῦ ὑψίστου, τά τε ἱερὰ * εἶναι ἐν ἀσυλίᾳ καὶ ἀναπέμπεσθαι εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ ἀποδίδοσθαι τοῖς ἀποδοχεῦσιν Ἱεροσολύμων, ἐγγύας τε μὴ ὁμολογεῖν αὐτοὺς ἐν σάββασιν ἢ τῇ πρὸ αὐτῆς παρασκευῇ ἀπὸ ὥρας ἐνάτης.  ἐὰν δέ τις φωραθῇ κλέπτων τὰς ἱερὰς βίβλους αὐτῶν ἢ τὰ ἱερὰ χρήματα ἔκ τε σαββατείου ἔκ τε ἀνδρῶνος, εἶναι αὐτὸν ἱερόσυλον καὶ τὸν βίον αὐτοῦ ἐνεχθῆναι εἰς τὸ δημόσιον τῶν Ῥωμαίων.  τό τε ψήφισμα τὸ δοθέν μοι ὑπ᾽ αὐτῶν ὑπὲρ τῆς ἐμῆς εὐσεβείας ἧς ἔχω πρὸς πάντας ἀνθρώπους καὶ ὑπὲρ Γαΐου Μαρκίου Κηνσωρίνου καὶ τοῦτο τὸ διάταγμα κελεύω ἀνατεθῆναι ἐν ἐπισημοτάτῳ τόπῳ τῷ γενηθέντι μοι ὑπὸ τοῦ κοινοῦ τῆς Ἀσίας ἐν Ἀγκύρῃ. ἐὰν δέ τις παραβῇ τι τῶν προειρημένων, δώσει δίκην οὐ μετρίαν. ἐστηλογραφήθη ἐν τῷ Καίσαρος ναῷ.’</tei-p>
					</tei-div>

chapters.Latin:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-3" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="166"><tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num166" id="latin-book16-num166" data-origname="p" data-processed="">caesar norbano flacco salutem, iudaei qui antiquam consuetudinem solent pecunias sacras ad hierosolimam transmittere sine inpedimento hoc faciant, haec quidem caesar.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.English:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-3" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="166"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num166" xml:id="english-book16-num166" id="english-book16-num166" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[166]</tei-num> "Caesar to Norbanus Flaccus, sendeth greeting. Let those Jews, how many soever they be, who have been used, according to their ancient custom, to send their sacred money to Jerusalem, do the same freely." These were the decrees of Caesar.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.Greek:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-3" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="166"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num166" xml:id="greek-book16-num166" id="greek-book16-num166" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> ‘Καῖσαρ Νωρβανῷ Φλάκκῳ χαίρειν. Ἰουδαῖοι ὅσοι ποτ᾽ οὖν εἰσίν, οἳ δι᾽ ἀρχαίαν συνήθειαν εἰώθασιν χρήματά τε ἱερὰ φέροντες ἀναπέμπειν ἀκωλύτως τοῦτο ποιείτωσαν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.’ καὶ ταῦτα μὲν Καῖσαρ.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>

chapters.Latin:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-4" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="167"><tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num167" id="latin-book16-num167" data-origname="p" data-processed="">agrippa uero scripsit per iudaeis hoc modo. Agrippe magistratibus senatui populoque phesiorum salutem. Pecuniarum sacrarumque in hierosolimorum templum transmittuntur, diligentiam et custodiam in asya iudaeos habere praecipio secundum patrium morem. Hos autem qui sacras pecunias iudaeorum auferunt et ad asilium confugiunt, iubeo de trai iudeisque tradi quod iure etiam sacrilegii detrahuntur. Scripsi uero silano magistratum gerenti ne sabbato iudaei conpellantur uadimonia prebere.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.English:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-4" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="167"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num167" xml:id="english-book16-num167" id="english-book16-num167" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[167]</tei-num> Agrippa also did himself write after the manner following, on behalf of the Jews: "Agrippa, to the magistrates, senate, and people of the Ephesians, sendeth greeting. I will that the care and custody of the sacred money that is carried to the temple at Jerusalem be left to the Jews of Asia, to do with it according to their ancient custom; and that such as steal that sacred money of the Jews, and fly to a sanctuary, shall be taken thence and delivered to the Jews, by the same law that sacrilegious persons are taken thence. I have also written to Sylvanus the praetor, that no one compel the Jews to come before a judge on the sabbath day."</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.Greek:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-4" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="167"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num167" xml:id="greek-book16-num167" id="greek-book16-num167" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> Ἀγρίππας δὲ καὶ αὐτὸς ἔγραψεν ὑπὲρ τῶν Ἰουδαίων τὸν τρόπον τοῦτον: ‘Ἀγρίππας Ἐφεσίων ἄρχουσι βουλῇ δήμῳ χαίρειν. τῶν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν τὸ ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἀναφερομένων ἱερῶν χρημάτων τὴν ἐπιμέλειαν καὶ φυλακὴν βούλομαι τοὺς ἐν Ἀσίᾳ Ἰουδαίους ποιεῖσθαι κατὰ τὰ πάτρια.  τούς τε κλέπτοντας ἱερὰ γράμματα τῶν Ἰουδαίων καταφεύγοντάς τε εἰς τὰς ἀσυλίας βούλομαι ἀποσπᾶσθαι καὶ παραδίδοσθαι τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις, ᾧ δικαίῳ ἀποσπῶνται οἱ ἱερόσυλοι. ἔγραψα δὲ καὶ Σιλανῷ τῷ στρατηγῷ, ἵνα σάββασιν μηδεὶς ἀναγκάζῃ Ἰουδαῖον ἐγγύας ὁμολογεῖν.’</tei-p>
					</tei-div>

chapters.Latin:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-5" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="169"><tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num169" id="latin-book16-num169" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Marcus agrippa quirinensium magistratibus senatui et populo salutem. Iudaei qui per cirenen quibus iam augustus scriptis in libia fabio magistratum gerenti aliisque ibi prouintiae procuratoribus quatenus sine inpedimento paecuniae hierosolimis secundum morem suum transmittantur. Nunc me interpellauerunt qui ab aliquibus<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb> calumpniatoribus affliguntur ocasione tributorum quae nequaquam debent et prohibentur solemnia sua per agere quo<tei-gap data-origname="gap" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-gap> nullo modo impediri admoneo. Sed et in quas sacras pecunias ciues ab eis abstulerunt has ipsis reddi praetio et in reliquo corrigi net alia committantur.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.English:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-5" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="169"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num169" xml:id="english-book16-num169" id="english-book16-num169" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[169]</tei-num> "Marcus Agrippa to the magistrates, senate, and people of Cyrene, sendeth greeting. The Jews of Cyrene have interceded with me for the performance of what Augustus sent orders about to Flavius, the then praetor of Libya, and to the other procurators of that province, that the sacred money may be sent to Jerusalem freely, as hath been their custom from their forefathers, they complaining that they are abused by certain informers, and under pretense of taxes which were not due, are hindered from sending them, which I command to be restored without any diminution or disturbance given to them. And if any of that sacred money in the cities be taken from their proper receivers, I further enjoin, that the same be exactly returned to the Jews in that place."</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.Greek:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-5" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="169"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num169" xml:id="greek-book16-num169" id="greek-book16-num169" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> ‘Μᾶρκος Ἀγρίππας Κυρηναίων ἄρχουσιν βουλῇ δήμῳ χαίρειν. οἱ ἐν Κυρήνῃ Ἰουδαῖοι, ὑπὲρ ὧν ἤδη ὁ Σεβαστὸς ἔπεμψεν πρὸς τὸν ἐν Λιβύῃ στρατηγὸν τόντε ὄντα Φλάβιον καὶ πρὸς τοὺς ἄλλους τοὺς τῆς ἐπαρχίας ἐπιμελουμένους, ἵνα ἀνεπικωλύτως ἀναπέμπηται τὰ ἱερὰ χρήματα εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, ὡς ἔστιν αὐτοῖς πάτριον,  ἐνέτυχόν μοι νῦν, ὡς ὑπό τινων συκοφαντῶν ἐπηρεαζόμενοι καὶ ὡς ἐν προφάσει τελῶν μὴ ὀφειλομένων κωλύοιντο: οἷς ἀποκαθιστάνειν κατὰ μηδένα τρόπον ἐνοχλουμένοις, καὶ εἴ τινων ἱερὰ χρήματα ἀφῄρηνται τῶν πόλεων τοὺς εἰς ταῦτα ἀποκεκριμένους καὶ ταῦτα διορθώσασθαι τοῖς ἐκεῖ Ἰουδαίοις κελεύω.’</tei-p>
					</tei-div>

chapters.Latin:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-6" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="171"><tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num171" id="latin-book16-num171" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Gaius norbanus flaccus proconsul sardiniensium magistratibus et senatui salutem. Caesar scripsit mihi praecipiens nequaquam iudaeos prohiberi patria consuetudine pecunias colligentes ad hierosolimam transmittere. Scripsi ergo uobis ut sciatis quem caesar et ego sic uolumus</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.English:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-6" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="171"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num171" xml:id="english-book16-num171" id="english-book16-num171" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[171]</tei-num> "Caius Norbanus Flaccus, proconsul, to the magistrates of the Sardians, sendeth greeting. Caesar hath written to me, and commanded me not to forbid the Jews, how many soever they be, from assembling together according to the custom of their forefathers, nor from sending their money to Jerusalem. I have therefore written to you, that you may know that both Caesar and I would have you act accordingly."</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.Greek:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-6" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="171"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num171" xml:id="greek-book16-num171" id="greek-book16-num171" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> ‘Γάιος Νωρβανὸς Φλάκκος ἀνθύπατος Σαρδιανῶν ἄρχουσι χαίρειν. Καῖσάρ μοι ἔγραψεν κελεύων μὴ κωλύεσθαι τοὺς Ἰουδαίους ὅσα ἂν ὦσιν κατὰ τὸ πάτριον αὐτοῖς ἔθος συναγαγόντες χρήματα ἀναπέμπειν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα. ἔγραψα οὖν ὑμῖν, ἵν᾽ εἰδῆτε, ὅτι Καῖσαρ κἀγὼ οὕτως θέλομεν γίνεσθαι.’</tei-p>
					</tei-div>

chapters.Latin:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-7" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="172"><tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num172" id="latin-book16-num172" data-origname="p" data-processed="">nihilominus et iulius proconsul scripsit ita ephesiorum magistratibus senatui et populo salutem. Per asiam iudaei habitantes idibus <tei-expan data-origname="expan" data-processed="">februaris</tei-expan> ephesi mihi iudicanti demonstrauerunt caesarem augustum et agrippam concessisse eis propriis uti legibus immo et pri micias quas singuli eorum si uoluntate piaetatis causa quam in deo habent solent transmittere, habeant licentiam sine inpedimento hoc agere. Petierunt autem ut ego similiter cum decretis a caesare uel agrippa meam sententiam confirmarem. Volo igitur uos cognoscere quoniam decretis augustu et agrippae parens, praecipi eos uti et seruare sine inpedimento sua solemnia.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.English:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-7" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="172"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num172" xml:id="english-book16-num172" id="english-book16-num172" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[172]</tei-num> Nor did Julius Antonius, the proconsul, write otherwise. "To the magistrates, senate, and people of the Ephesians, sendeth greeting. As I was dispensing justice at Ephesus, on the Ides of February, the Jews that dwell in Asia demonstrated to me that Augustus and Agrippa had permitted them to use their own laws and customs, and to offer those their first-fruits, which every one of them freely offers to the Deity on account of piety, and to carry them in a company together to Jerusalem without disturbance. They also petitioned me that I also would confirm what had been granted by Augustus and Agrippa by my own sanction. I would therefore have you take notice, that according to the will of Augustus and Agrippa, I permit them to use and do according to the customs of their forefathers without disturbance."</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
chapters.Greek:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-7" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="172"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num172" xml:id="greek-book16-num172" id="greek-book16-num172" data-origname="p" data-processed=""> Οὐδὲν ἧττον καὶ Ἰούλιος Ἀντώνιος ἀνθύπατος ἔγραψεν ‘Ἐφεσίων ἄρχουσιν βουλῇ δήμῳ χαίρειν. οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ κατοικοῦντες Ἰουδαῖοι εἰδοῖς Φεβρουαρίοις δικαιοδοτοῦντί μοι ἐν Ἐφέσῳ ὑπέδειξαν Καίσαρα τὸν Σεβαστὸν καὶ Ἀγρίππαν συγκεχωρηκέναι αὐτοῖς χρῆσθαι τοῖς ἰδίοις νόμοις καὶ ἔθεσιν, ἀπαρχάς τε, ἃς ἕκαστος αὐτῶν ἐκ τῆς ἰδίας προαιρέσεως εὐσεβείας ἕνεκα τῆς πρὸς τὸ θεῖον * ἀνακομιδῆς συμπορευομένους ποιεῖν ἀνεμποδίστως.  ᾔτουν τε, ὅπως κἀγὼ ὁμοίως τοῖς ὑπὸ τοῦ Σεβαστοῦ καὶ Ἀγρίππα δοθεῖσιν τὴν ἐμὴν γνώμην βεβαιώσω. ὑμᾶς οὖν βούλομαι εἰδέναι ἐν τοῖς τοῦ Σεβαστοῦ καὶ Ἀγρίππα βουλήμασιν συνεπιτρέπειν αὐτοῖς χρῆσθαι καὶ ποιεῖν κατὰ τὰ πάτρια χωρὶς ἐμποδισμοῦ.’</tei-p>
					</tei-div>

chapters.Latin:
<tei-div type="subchapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-16-Subchapter-6-8" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="174"><tei-div2 n="11" type="chapter" data-origname="div2" data-processed=""><tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num174" id="latin-book16-num174" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Haec ideo explanauimus quoniam conscripta nostra amplius apud graecos uenturas ut demonstrem eis quia cunctum honorem ab initio impetrantes nihil ex patriis legibus prohibiti sumus a magistratibus agere sed et defendebamur religionem et honores in deo seruantes, quorum facio sepius mentionem ut mutatis <tei-expan data-origname="expan" data-processed="">saeculi</tei-expan> odiis causae quae nobis ob hoc uel illis inracionabiliter insertae sunt euellantur. Nam legibus hisdem nulla gens semper utitur dum et per ciuitates multa religionis differentia seruetur. Iustitia uero cunctis hominibus similiter studetur, quae commoda graecis uel barbaris existit, de qua nostrae leges multam rationem habentes omnes homines <tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00398.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="197v" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb> debent nos ut amicos et hospites amplecti, nam oportet non differentia nos religionum alienos facere, sed non seruatus benignitatis affectus, quae omnium hominum communem uitam poterit custodire redeo uero ad reliquam monumem ta conscriptionis.</tei-p>
				</tei-div2>
				<tei-div2 n="12" type="chapter" data-origname="div2" data-processed="">
					</tei-div2></tei-div>
chapters.English:
